title: Session gossip propagation and TTL butterfly notes
content:
Summary:
This is a working note for a lightweight session metadata propagation protocol were calling the "TTL butterfly". Goal: keep ephemeral session state (session prewarm tokens, last-access vector, soft-affinity hints) roughly consistent across a small set of edge proxies and regional routers without a heavy central store or synchronous replication. Intended for mid-frequency session updates (1-10 updates/sec per session peak) where eventual bounded staleness is acceptable but full divergence causes degraded UX (repeated cold starts, duplicate prewarms).

Why gossip?
- Many edge nodes, transient client connections, and variable routing make point-to-point sync brittle.
- Gossip provides graceful amplification across a small neighborhood while bounding network load.
- We only need small vectors (timestamp, prewarm-score, affinity-token, short KV metadata).

High-level idea (TTL butterfly):
1) Each update emits a short gossip packet with a short TTL (hop-count) and an epoch id.
2) Receiving nodes merge update into local session shard and forward with TTL-1 to a bounded peer set (not full cluster).
3) Butterfly pattern: peers chosen by layered fanout so updates propagate along 2-3 waves rather than full-cluster flood.
4) Soft decay: metadata carries 'freshness' weight; older tags are gradually demoted and can trigger prewarm expiry.

Packet shape (sketch, compact):
- session_id (string)
- epoch (int, monotonic per session origin)
- origin_node (node id)
- created_at (ms)
- ttl_hops (int)
- payload_keys (list e.g. ["prewarm", "affinity", "last_user_op"])
- payload_blob (base64 or compact k/v pairs)
- vector_score (float 0..1) // optional scoring for priority merge

Merge policy notes:
- If incoming epoch > stored epoch -> accept and replace relevant keys.
- If epoch == stored epoch -> per-key last-writer-by-timestamp.
- If epoch < stored epoch -> ignore unless vector_score exceeds a promotion threshold (to recover from missing updates).

Peer selection heuristics (for forwarding):
- Prefer nodes in same region but different AZ.
- Prefer previously observed affinity peers for this session (if present).
- Add small probability of random peer to reduce partition bias (1-2%).
- Bound fanout: 3 peers for first wave, 2 for subsequent waves.

Butterfly topology ascii (2 waves):
client -> edgeA -> {edgeB, edgeC, edgeD} -> {edgeE, edgeF}
TTL hops: 2 -> first wave forwards to fanout set, second wave completes local neighborhood.

Consistency and staleness guarantees (informal):
- Expectation: majority of neighborhood sees update within ~50-200ms for intra-region, 200-600ms cross-region depending on fanout and RTT.
- Tunables: ttl_hops, fanout size, inter-gossip timer, promotion threshold.
- Tradeoff: larger fanout reduces tail staleness but increases bandwidth and amplification on hot sessions.

Failure modes & mitigations:
- Hot-shot storms: a session that updates at 1000/sec could overwhelm gossip; mitigations: per-session rate limit + coalesce window (50-200ms), sampling (only 1 in N updates gossiped) and local delta compression.
- Partitioned neighborhoods: add background reconciliation via lite pull from directory service every N minutes (e.g., 5min) for sessions with active prewarm flags.
- Duplicate prewarms: dedupe by origin epoch and origin_node hints.

Operational signals to capture:
- per-session gossip bytes/sec, per-node forwarded packets, average propagation latency to neighborhood percentile (p50/p95), number of sessions hitting background reconciliation, stale-prewarm ratio (requests that still saw cold start despite prewarm flag).

Experiment plan (A/B):
- A: baseline current static cache TTL approach on 10% traffic.
- B: TTL-butterfly with ttl_hops=2, fanout=3 and coalesce window 100ms on 10% traffic.
- Metrics: cold-start rate, added bandwidth, tail latency, and number of background reconciles.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to encode cryptographic anti-spoofing cheaply? HMAC of payload with node key? Adds CPU but prevents malicious spoofing in multi-tenant edge.
- Should we support negative-acks (explicit invalidate) or expiry-only? Invalidates propagate similarly but increase churn.
- Backpressure strategy: when node overloaded, drop low-score gossips vs drop random; which correlates better with UX?

Notes to implementers:
- Keep packet size < 512 bytes typical; prefer key lists instead of full blobs where possible.
- Store per-session merged blob in a tiny LRU with expiration (match prewarm expiry). Consider passive eviction when storage > X MB.
- Add a lightweight debug flag to force full-wave propagation for a single session (dev/testing).

References & links:
- Jira INF-1987: session prewarm improvements (linked above)
- PR 412: small peer-selection helper & test harness

Last thoughts: this is intentionally heuristic-heavy. The aim is practical: reduce UX cold starts without a new global store. TTL butterfly should be parametrizable per-tenant (enterprise tenants may want stricter staleness and larger fanout).

Sofia
